question: Should OpenClaw add native context-pressure escalation for subagent sessions, and if so should it be observe-only notification, parent-routed recovery, or automatic recovery?
rationale: The code has context and lineage data, but the threshold, notification target, and recovery authority are product/API decisions that affect subagent semantics and config surface.

options.title: Narrow native alert first
options.body: Add a single diagnostics/subagent-status context-pressure signal that notifies the requester/operator, with recovery remaining manual until live proof justifies automation.

options.title: Parent-routed recovery
options.body: Let saturated child sessions emit a parent-visible event that the requester can use to reroute or restart work, accepting a larger behavior/API change.

options.title: Keep external monitoring
options.body: Leave fleet-level saturation policy to operator scripts or plugins and keep core limited to reporting context usage.

recommendation.title: Narrow native alert first
recommendation.body: Add a single diagnostics/subagent-status context-pressure signal that notifies the requester/operator, with recovery remaining manual until live proof justifies automation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses sessions_spawn semantics, subagent completion delivery, and diagnostic recovery thresholds where this history shows the strongest ownership trail.
